original_card.question: Does one explicit extension of the connector alphabet offer a favorable completed budget?
methods: Construct and charge a legal extra operation on a minimal instance.
Prove a target-specific bound after adding one specified operation family.
original_card.acceptance_gate: State which fixed-alphabet premise changes and charge its implementation; do not declare it free. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Reproduce the 945-pairing control, then read Exact interface to list the allowed calls.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Add exactly one legally priced operation and test a tiny dirty-input instance before enumerating larger cases.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A new legal connector operation could change recursive interface cost; a larger census in the same alphabet is a separate side result.
allowed_variations: Choose one additional operation and a small source count for its first counterexample.
scope_change_triggers: Keeping the alphabet and only increasing the source count; record this as a changed assignment.
Extending a source-count census without naming a supplier/interface decision it could change; audit #2973 pruning concerns before relying on the affected predecessor exclusions.

actual_scope: Prove exact paid cost n for every ordinary rank-one target in M_n(M_m(K)), m>=2, for every field K and every positive role count n.
scope_change_reason: This takes the arbitrary-role noncommutative cost question of PR4276 and PR4265 as a singular matrix-algebra side result. It does not add an operation to the original connector alphabet or claim a complete physical budget.
bottleneck_link: A formal exact-cost family in the relaxed algebra-valued alphabet. It identifies the full n-call cost of low ordinary-rank singular targets; it supplies no native coefficient preparation or recursive supplier.
stop_rule: Stop at the first written exact family and a bounded literal-word verification; leave higher-rank and native questions open.
evidence: PROOF.md gives an all-field rank-loss lower bound and n-factor construction. verify.py enumerates rank-one targets over F2, F3 and F4, checks literal factors, block-matrix products and independent vector action, plus rejection and sharpness controls.
author: Nick Petalas
ai_assistance: Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

open_questions.question: Which targets of ordinary rank 2 through m-1 have paid cost n over M_m(K)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: This would locate the first obstruction to extending the singular exact-cost family beyond rank one.
open_questions.first_step: For m=3 and n=2, test whether an ordinary rank-two target has an input block restriction retaining its complete row-space rank, using PR4276 Corollary C.
open_questions.blocked_by: A rank-one row always has a nonzero block; the higher-rank simultaneous block condition is not automatic.

open_questions.question: Can one literal native producer and consumer realize these algebra-valued column replacements at their charged cost?
open_questions.why_it_matters: A formal word does not price a recursive supplier.
open_questions.first_step: Choose one actual matrix coefficient and record its preparation, overwrite, routing and restoration contract before any construction expansion.
open_questions.blocked_by: All native implementation and complete invoice costs are unknown.
